reviewer.selectedModelRationale: Approved independent reasoning challenger remains the best fit for Phase 0 correctness, traceability, boundary and omission review. gpt-5.6-sol is the Phase 0 author model and cannot be used for independent AFF-A review; gpt-5.3-codex is more implementation/testing oriented.
reviewer.runtimeIdentityEvidence: Active task launcher binding explicitly and exactly enforced gpt-5.5 for this review invocation.

confirmedItems: Governing files reviewed: AFF operating contract, lifecycle, AFF-A profile, active model plan, and canonical Phase 0 hash manifest.
Reviewer and author actual model IDs differ: reviewer gpt-5.5; author gpt-5.6-sol.
Phase 0 content stays within coordination and does not assert approved requirements, architecture, Azure service selection, legal obligation, deployment, test result, or human approval.
Evidence-backed known facts are traceable to the normalised source and framed as source statements rather than approved requirements.
Rendered HTML is self-contained, uses inline CSS, has no external scripts or CDNs, links large evidence rather than embedding it, and materially matches the authoritative Markdown.
Shared decision, risk, and regulatory records are concise and align with Phase 0 boundaries.

findings.title: Listed SHA-256 hashes were not independently verifiable in this review runtime
evidence: Canonical manifest lists nine SHA-256 values and invocation supplies manifest SHA-256 8cd64963807398f3a8e9ba9b392f5ca98c7ebf5c1a4e89cb34d79e51e98899ac.
Available read-only review tooling exposed file content but no byte-level checksum operation.
PDF evidence is compressed binary and was only partially viewable.
findings.impact: AFF-A cannot truthfully confirm that the reviewed bytes exactly match every listed SHA-256 or the supplied canonical manifest hash; the phase gate depends on hash-bound final reviews over unchanged subject artifacts.
findings.requiredAction: Re-invoke review in a context where AFF-A can independently verify each artifact and manifest SHA-256, or add retained, reviewable hash-generation evidence and regenerate the canonical manifest as needed.

findings.title: Active run journal is cited but omitted from the canonical reviewed hash set
evidence: 0-coordination/stratton-coordination.md lists ../stratton-run-journal.jsonl as an active shared record and append-only Phase 0 lifecycle evidence.
stratton-run-journal.jsonl exists and records case identity, phase entry, source ingestion, normalisation, and model-plan creation events.
findings.impact: Lifecycle evidence used by the Phase 0 artifact is outside the hash-bound review set, so the review cannot bind that cited evidence to an unchanged hash.
findings.requiredAction: Include stratton-run-journal.jsonl in the canonical Phase 0 hash manifest, or remove/correct the Phase 0 artifact's reliance on it. Regenerate affected artifacts and hashes, then re-invoke review.

findings.title: Normalisation method claim lacks retained validation evidence
evidence: stratton-input-inventory.json states that selectable text and tables were extracted programmatically and checked against rendered page images.
The manifest retains the PDF and normalised Markdown but no conversion log or rendered-page comparison evidence.
findings.impact: The normalised text is usable for Phase 0, but the process-quality claim is stronger than the retained evidence independently demonstrates.
findings.requiredAction: Either qualify the method statement as an AFF-0 assertion or retain concise conversion/check evidence in a reviewed artifact if that claim remains material.

verdictRationale: The Phase 0 narrative is generally disciplined and boundary-safe, but the gate cannot open because hash verification is incomplete and a cited active lifecycle record is outside the canonical hash set.
requiredAction: AFF-0 should remediate the hash and evidence issues, regenerate the affected canonical hash manifest and any affected rendered artifacts, then directly re-invoke AFF-A for round 2.
